item.title: Multimodal Large Language Models and Agentic AI in Transportation
item.content:encoded:
Yuhuan Lu, Macao Polytechnic University

Yuanfang Zhu, Nagoya University

Jun Zhuang, Boise State University

Guoqiang Mao, Southeast University

This special issue addresses how multimodal large language models and agentic AI are transforming transportation systems. By combining language understanding with visual, spatial, and sensor data, these technologies enable more intelligent autonomous driving, traffic management, and mobility services. The focus is on advancing safety, efficiency, accessibility, and sustainability across transportation networks.

The issue tackles key challenges in deploying these systems in transportation, including grounding language in real traffic scenes, handling diverse sensor inputs, generalizing across different cities and conditions, and ensuring trustworthy decision-making in safety-critical scenarios. Submissions should connect foundational AI methods to rigorous evaluation and real-world transportation outcomes.

The special issue welcomes research on architectures, algorithms, datasets, benchmarks, and deployment of multimodal and LLM-based systems across autonomous driving, traffic prediction, infrastructure coordination, public transit, and freight logistics. Research addressing safety, fairness, privacy, human oversight, and sustainability in transportation AI is also welcomed.

Appel publié par Expert Systems. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Multimodal Foundation Models for Transportation
  • Transportation-Focused LLMs and Knowledge-Grounded Reasoning
  • Vision-Language-Action Models for Connected and Automated Driving
  • Multimodal Traffic Perception and Situation Understanding
  • Agentic AI and Multi-Agent Transportation Intelligence
  • Traffic Forecasting and Mobility Demand Modeling
  • Transportation Operations, Logistics, and Mobility Services
  • Digital Twins, Simulation, and Generative Traffic Modeling
  • Evaluation, Robustness, Safety, and Explainability
  • Responsible, Human-Centered, and Sustainable Transportation AI

item.title: Mathematical Foundations for Trustworthy AI Applications in Transportation Systems
item.content:encoded:
This special issue focuses on the mathematical and computational foundations necessary for developing trustworthy artificial intelligence applications in transportation systems. As AI increasingly influences critical transportation decisions affecting safety, efficiency, and equity, there is an urgent need for rigorous mathematical frameworks that ensure these systems are reliable, interpretable, and accountable.

The special issue welcomes contributions that advance the theoretical understanding and practical implementation of trustworthy AI in transportation. This includes work on mathematical models that enhance transparency, ensure robustness against adversarial attacks, quantify uncertainties, and address fairness concerns in transportation algorithms and systems.

Submissions should demonstrate how mathematical and computational approaches contribute to building trustworthy AI systems that stakeholders can understand, verify, and depend upon for critical transportation applications.

Appel publié par Transportation Research Part B Methodological. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Mathematical frameworks for explainability and interpretability in transportation AI
  • Formal verification and validation methods for autonomous vehicles
  • Trustworthy machine learning algorithms for traffic prediction and management
  • Robustness and adversarial resilience in transportation systems
  • Uncertainty quantification in AI-based transportation applications
  • Fairness and bias mitigation in transportation decision-making systems
  • Privacy-preserving techniques in transportation data analytics
  • Game-theoretic approaches to multi-agent transportation systems
  • Causal inference methods for transportation research
  • Probabilistic and Bayesian methods in transportation AI

Timeline

  • December 1, 2026: Full paper submission deadline

item.title: Rethinking Transit-Oriented Development: Territorial restructuring, intermodality and governance

item.title: Transportation Ecology
item.content:encoded:
This special issue focuses on the intersection of transportation systems and ecological processes. It addresses the complex relationships between human mobility, infrastructure development, and natural ecosystems, examining both the negative impacts of transportation on biodiversity and environmental quality, as well as solutions that balance transportation needs with ecological conservation.
